title: Where international students live in Germany
description: Dormitory, shared flat, studio or host family: the housing options for students in Germany, what each costs and how to find one from abroad.
html:
Finding a place to live is usually the last big task before departure, and for many students the most stressful one. Germany has a real shortage of student housing in the big cities, but there are more options than most newcomers realise. This guide walks through them, with rough costs and the practical trade-offs.

Student residences

The cheapest option is a room in a residence run by the local student services organisation (Studierendenwerk). Rents typically run from about €250 to €450 a month including utilities, which is far below the private market in cities like Munich or Frankfurt. The catch is demand: waiting lists in popular cities can be a semester or longer, so apply the moment you have your admission letter, not after you arrive. Private residences exist too, with nicer rooms and shorter waits, but at roughly double the price.

Shared flats

The shared flat (WG, short for Wohngemeinschaft) is the classic German student arrangement: two to five people renting a flat together, each with a private room and a shared kitchen and bathroom. It is the most common choice among international students because it combines affordable rent, a ready-made social circle and language practice. Expect €350 to €600 a month for a room, more in Munich. Flatmates usually interview candidates, so a short, friendly message in German or English and some flexibility on viewing times go a long way.

A flat of your own

A studio or one-bedroom flat gives you privacy and quiet, at a price. Outside the largest cities a small flat starts around €500 a month plus utilities; in Munich, Frankfurt or Hamburg it is closer to €900. Landlords typically ask for proof of income or a guarantor, a credit report and a deposit of up to three months' rent. For a first-year student without a German income history, this is the hardest option to secure from abroad.

Host families

Living with a German family is common for language students and short courses. You get a furnished room, often meals, and daily language practice. Prices vary widely; language schools usually arrange placements and quote around €400 to €700 a month with half board.

Where to search

The student services organisation of your university is the first stop for residences. For rooms and flats, the large national listing portals and dedicated shared-flat platforms are where most offers appear. Platforms that specialise in international tenants let you book from abroad with verified landlords, which removes the biggest risk: paying a deposit for a room that does not exist. Never transfer money before you have seen the room or the landlord has been verified by a platform.

If you need something for the first weeks

Many students arrive without a permanent room and stay in a hostel, a short-term sublet or temporary student housing for the first two to four weeks. This is normal. It gives you time to view rooms in person, which improves your chances considerably. Just make sure the temporary address can be used for your city registration, or that you can register once you move.
